title: check format's swift arm invoked swift-format with a flag it has never had
body:
# 0010: check format's swift arm invoked swift-format with a flag it has never had

## Tags

swift, gates, D21, false-green, determinate-zero, test-quality

## Summary

`_check_format_swift` ran `swift-format --lint "${files[@]}"`. swift-format dispatches on a SUBCOMMAND -- `lint`, or `format` as the default -- so `--lint` was being parsed as an unknown option of `format`, and the gate exited 1 with a usage dump the moment it was pointed at a project that has Swift in it.

The arm had never been executed. Devbin's own repository contains no `.swift` files, and the function returns green on its determinate-zero path before it reaches the command line. Every project in the first fleet that declares `swift` had likewise never run it against real sources. ST0002 WP-08 armed swift on Prolix -- a shipped iOS app, 80 Swift sources, on the App Store -- and it failed on the first line it was asked to do work on.

Its twin, `builtin_fmt_swift`, ran `swift-format --in-place`, which WORKS: `format` is the default subcommand, so the flag lands on the right parser by accident. That asymmetry is the reason this survived. The two lines stopped looking like a pair, so nothing invited the comparison that would have caught it.

## Reproduction

    $ cd <a project with Swift sources and `swift` in project.languages>
    $ bin/devbin check format
    ==> format -- swift
        78 file(s)
    Error: Unknown option '--lint'
    Usage: swift-format format [--in-place] [--configuration <configuration>] ...
    -> full log: tmp/check/<stamp>.FORMAT.out (exit 1)

And the corrected form, on the same file set:

    $ find . -name '*.swift' -not -path '*/build/*' -print0 | xargs -0 swift-format lint
    ./native/ios/Prolix/ProlixApp.swift:23:1: warning: [Indentation] indent by 2 spaces
    ... 633 findings

`swift-format --version` is 603.0.0. The subcommand structure is not new; there is no version of swift-format in which `--lint` was a flag of the default subcommand.

## Why the suite did not catch it

This is the more useful half of the finding.

`tests/unit/buildfmt.bats` covered the swift arm in three tests, and one of them asserted `ran:swift-format`. The helper they share is:

    fakebin() {
      printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "ran:%s args=$*"\n' "$name" >"$proj/fakebin/$name"
    }

A fake that accepts every argument and exits 0. It proves the binary was CALLED. It cannot prove it was called with arguments the binary accepts, and it will keep passing for any command line whatsoever, including one that is a syntax error to the real tool.

Worse, the file-set half of this same function had been reviewed twice and hardened twice -- once for macOS `xargs` not running its utility on empty input (the determinate-zero path, deliberately kept), once for NUL-delimiting after a path containing a newline was split in two (WP-13 delta review, finding 8). Both reviews were about which files get handed to the command. Neither was about the command. **The gate knew precisely which 78 files to pass to something that could not run.**

## The second defect, which the first fix walked straight into

Correcting the subcommand was not the fix. It was half of it, and the half that made things worse before they got better.

`swift-format lint` **exits 0 when it has findings.** They are warnings; only `--strict` promotes them to errors. So the corrected arm ran, examined 78 files, printed 633 findings to the terminal, and sealed GREEN:

    $ bin/prolix check format
    ==> format -- swift
        78 file(s)
    ./native/ios/Prolix/ProlixApp.swift:23:1: warning: [Indentation] indent by 2 spaces
    ... 633 of these ...
    verdict: tmp/check/20260810-2000.FORMAT.errors

    $ wc -l < tmp/check/20260810-2000.FORMAT.errors
    0

An empty `.errors` companion means the gate passed. A gate incapable of ever going red is a worse defect than one that always errors, because the hard error announces itself on first contact and this does not. Had the arm been declared working at the point it stopped throwing a usage dump, devbin would have shipped a swift formatting gate that could never fail, on the strength of having watched it "start working".

It was caught by the doctrine this project already holds: **read the seal, never the summary, and never the exit code.** The terminal was full of findings and the verdict file was empty. Nothing else in the run said anything was wrong.

Both halves are now in place: `swift-format lint --strict`.

## The determinate-zero interaction, which is the part worth generalising

Devbin's doctrine (issue 0003) is that a gate silently examining nothing is a false green, while a gate reporting a determinate "nothing to check" is legitimate and passes. That doctrine is right and is not changed by this.

But this is what it costs, stated plainly: **a legitimate empty run is still a run that proves nothing about the non-empty one.** `check format`'s swift arm was green in every project, in CI, and in 500-odd local suite runs, on a path that exits before the defect. The zero case and the non-zero case are different code, and only one of them had ever run.

Where a gate has a determinate-zero path, the suite needs at least one case that gets PAST it. That is now true here.

## Resolution

Fixed in the base, not patched at the project (ST0002 AC-08.3 requires exactly that).

- `lib/cmd/check`, `_check_format_swift`: `swift-format lint --strict "${files[@]}"`. Both halves -- the subcommand, and the promotion of findings to errors without which the gate cannot fail.
- `lib/cmd/fmt`, `builtin_fmt_swift`: `swift-format format --in-place`, with the default subcommand SPELLED OUT. It worked either way; spelling it out is what makes the two lines read as the pair D21 says they are, so the next person comparing them sees one shape.
- `tests/unit/buildfmt.bats`: two new tests, one per defect, each red-checked against the unfixed code first.
  - "the swift twins call swift-format the way swift-format is called" -- its fake mimics swift-format's argument grammar, dispatching on `lint` / `format` and erroring on anything else. Against the unfixed code it reproduces `Error: Unknown option '--lint'` verbatim.
  - "the swift gate FAILS on findings instead of printing them and passing" -- its fake models the exit-code contract: emit a finding, exit 0, and exit 1 only under `--strict`. Against the subcommand-only fix it reports "Expected failure but got exit code 0", which is the false green in one line.

The general lesson for the rest of the corpus's fakes: a stub that accepts everything tests the caller's plumbing, not the caller's correctness. Where a fake stands in for a tool with a real argument grammar, it should refuse what the tool refuses.

**The fleet is NOT re-vendored by this commit.** Installed projects keep the lib they have until their next `devbin upgrade`. Prolix takes it in WP-08 as part of arming its swift arms, which is where the defect was found.

## Notes

Prolix's own 633 lint findings are project dirt, not a devbin finding. They are recorded red and sized separately, per hv's arca_cli precedent -- a red baseline arm is recorded, not necessarily fixed -- and emphatically NOT fixed inside a migration work package: `fmt swift` would rewrite 80 source files of a released application in a commit whose subject is a launcher.
